title: Working Sinatra's television show and tours with Nelson Riddle
summary: He worked a year on Sinatra's show and flew weekend concerts with Riddle; Sinatra kept him on after he asked for work.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working with Sinatra: bands, Vegas and the Sands

blocks.x: And you also worked here -- on television, you were on the Sinatra show, right?
Oh, yes; I did the Sinatra show for a whole year.
That was -- which one? Was that the Sinatra Chesterfield Show?
Was that the one he did for Chesterfield up on Vine Street in the fifties?

For dates, don't ask me -- because I cannot keep up with dates, anyhow. But whenever Sinatra had the whole television show, I worked with him, and while I worked with him, because ask him about it -- I told him, I said, one day I record. I used to record with ...
Nelson Riddle, which was the band with Frank Sinatra, you know? And in one of those intermission things, to get some coffee and so on, I told Frank, I said,

"Frank, I wish you would put me up on something, because these people are keeping me back and I would like to be working or playing somewhere." So he said to me, "I'm gonna try to do my best; I'm gonna keep you up there. You're gonna be working with me."
And it happened that way. I recorded everything he wanted to record; I was in the band with Nelson Riddle.

With Nelson Riddle, and when we went - we used to go on a trip to do Saturdays and Sundays, to fly, you know, and do two states on Saturday and two states on Sunday. Friday matinee here in one state, and then get on the airplane after the concert and go to another state for the night show. Things like that. And on Sunday, too -- we did that on Sundays, too.
That was with Frank Sinatra, huh?
You also did a Nat Cole show, too.

I never will forget one time it was a plane coming through, you know? And they knew I was scared of planes; I was pretty tight, and Frank said to me, "You see that plane over there? Don't worry about it -- it's going to go through ..."
You were on a plane when this happened, right? You were in the air?
Yeah. I was in the air.
